**Other artists whose pop, R&B, or mainstream‑jazz hits found regular rotation on smooth‑jazz stations (besides Kenny G and Dave Koz, the “A Smooth Jazz Christmas” de‑facto star)**  

| Artist | Notable crossover titles | Why they landed on the dial |
|--------|------------------------|--------------------------------|
| **Anita Baker** | “Sweet Love,” “I’m Gonna Be (500 Miles)” | Slow‑roll R&B/neo‑soul ballads that blended moody soul with a relaxed groove that fit the smooth‑jazz aesthetic. |
| **Sade** | “Smooth Operator,” “No Ordinary Love” | Soul‑pop tracks with understated jazz‑inspired horn arrangements and a languid groove. |
| **Al Jarreau** | “You Make Me Feel Brand New,” “Sweet Love” | Vocal‑focussed R&B that was often stripped of the vocal or turned into melodic instrumentals for a jazz‑friendly feel. |
| **Grover Washington Jr.** | “Winelight,” “Just the Two of Us” (with Billie Holiday) | Late‑night instrumental pieces that meshed pop hooks with smooth‑jazz saxophone lines. |
| **David Sanborn** | “Pick Up the Pieces,” “Rosanna” | Flute‑driven tunes that carried a pop‑mellifluous hook, getting airplay both in jazz and contemporary‑hits sets. |
| **George Benson** (George Benson) | “Breezin’,” “The Way You Do” | Highly melodic, sax‑heavy pop‑jazz staples that bridged pop and jazz. |
| **Boney James** | “Help Me,” “A Simple Man” | Contemporary sax‑centric compositions that charted on smooth‑jazz airplay charts while retaining pop‑friendly hooks. |
| **Patti LaBelle** (remixed versions) | “If You Love Me” (smooth‑ballad remix) | R&B ballad stretched into a more laid‑back, instrumental‑friendly mix for the radio. |
| **Bobby Caldwell** | “What You Won’t Do for Love” | Classic R&B hit often re‑arranged for smooth‑jazz’s mellow groove. |
| **Spyro Gyra** | “Morning Dance,” “Best of the Ballads” | Jazz‑fusion outfit with clear pop outlines; their tunes were frequently etched into smooth‑jazz playlists. |
| **Chuck Mangione** | “Feels So Good” | Catchy, high‑energy trumpet‑led track that bridged pop and jazz (also a staple on the Adult Contemporary charts). |

**Sources**  
- Wikipedia entry: *Smooth jazz* (lists Anita Baker, Sade, Al Jarreau, Grover Washington Jr., David Sanborn, and Kenny G as key crossover performers).  
- Wikipedia entry: *George Benson*, *Boney James*, *Bobby Caldwell*, etc.  
- Billboard and AllMusic discographies for individual tracks mentioned above.

These artists, along with Kenny G and Dave Koz, kept smooth‑jazz stations’ playlists varied, offering listeners familiar pop‑R&B grooves along with the characteristic mellow jazz tone.
